slides.title: Value Depends on Internal Collaboration Too
bullets: Most visible time is in the field, but value depends on internal reach
Partners include Medical Advisors, Market Access, Commercial, Clinical Development, Regulatory
Insight that never reaches the right audience hasn't really been generated

slides.title: Medical Advisors and the Strategy Team
bullets: Field insight is meant to flow into the Medical Plan and publication strategy
Works best as a genuinely two-way relationship
MSLs bring field intelligence up, Advisors bring strategic context down

slides.title: Strengthen the Dossier, the Right Way
bullets: Real-world evidence and clinical insight can strengthen a payer dossier
Must be shared through the correct, compliant channel
Never used as a workaround to influence pricing or access directly

slides.title: The Most Sensitive Relationship
bullets: Requires explicit understanding of the firewall rules from Module 1
Redirect questions that have drifted into commercial territory
Never share prescriber-level data or insight that could inform targeting

slides.title: When Insight Points to a Gap or a Risk
bullets: Relevant when field insight could inform future trial design
Safety observations go through pharmacovigilance channels
Always follow the formal adverse-event process without delay or filtering

slides.title: Three Habits of Effective Collaborators
bullets: Know which stakeholder actually owns which decision
Communicate insight in the format that stakeholder can act on
Build the working relationship before you urgently need it

takeaway.title: An MSL's field insight only counts once it reaches the right internal audience
bullets: Each internal partner needs insight shared through a different, appropriate channel
Commercial collaboration always respects firewall rules without exception
Relationship-building applies internally just as much as it does with KOLs
